children: The equity benchmark indices fell for the third straight day on Wednesday (September 9), with the Sensex dropping 813 points to 74,764 and the Nifty falling 204 points to 23,432.
The Nifty gave up the 23,500 mark as the market slipped to its lowest level in three months, with Brent crude crossing $100 a barrel. Here are five reasons behind today’s stock market fall:
The market decline came as Brent crude crossed the $100-a-barrel mark.
The fall was broad-based, with 38 of the 50 Nifty stocks closing lower. The Nifty Bank index fell 482 points to 56,296, while the Midcap index declined 323 points to 62,593.

Information technology (IT) stocks were the biggest laggards. Five of the top six Nifty losers were IT stocks, with Infosys, HCL Technologies, Tech Mahindra, Wipro and Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) among the top losers.
4. Insurance and HDFC Bank remain weak
Insurance stocks saw a sharp fall despite healthy August data, with HDFC Life Insurance declining 4%. HDFC Bank also remained weak, falling nearly 2% to close at a 52-week low.
Most realty stocks slipped, with Lodha and DLF among the top losers. Coforge closed off its lows but still ended 5% lower following the resignation of its chairman.
Adani Enterprises was the top Nifty gainer, rising more than 5% following a report on fundraising by Adani Airports. Adani Ports gained 3% after an order win for Paradip Port.

Power-related stocks also saw buying, with Adani Power, Bharat Heavy Electricals (BHEL) and Torrent Power among the top gainers. Among midcaps, Jindal Stainless (JSL), Paytm, Swiggy, Cummins and National Aluminium Company (NALCO) were among the top gainers.
From the Sensex basket, Max Healthcare Institute Ltd, Adani Ports & Special Economic Zone Ltd, Coal India Ltd, Tata Steel Ltd, Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd and Trent Ltd were the major gainers.
Infosys Ltd, HCL Technologies Ltd, Tech Mahindra Ltd, Wipro Ltd, Tata Consultancy Services Ltd and Hindustan Unilever Ltd were the biggest laggards.

title: Sensex falls 813 points, Nifty gives up 23,500: 5 reasons why market hit 3-month low
